source.title: Primate Orbitofrontal Cortex Codes Information Relevant for Managing Explore-Exploit Tradeoffs.

confidence_rationale: Primate single-unit recording showing OFC strongly encodes the IDENTITY of the chosen stimulus and that value coding is stimulus-SPECIFIC (not value independent of identity). This is direct support for what/where factorization: value is bound to object identity, so a goal seeded from the most-wanted object's identity latent is biologically faithful. Docked for macaque bandit task vs REE objects and for the seed-vs-code distinction.
failure_signatures: Value coding in OFC is stimulus-specific rather than identity-agnostic, but the chosen-value and exploration-bonus signals are encoded at only intermediate levels, so identity is not the sole determinant of the goal-relevant signal.
OFC also encodes choice location and environment value (at low levels), suggesting the seed for goal-directed behaviour integrates more than object identity alone.

mapping.source_claim_statement: OFC strongly encodes the identity of the chosen stimulus and the reward outcome, and OFC value coding is stimulus-specific rather than value independent of stimulus identity.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-346's bank.most_wanted(per_axis_drive) selects an object-IDENTITY latent (z_object) to seed z_goal; the finding that biological value is attached to specific stimulus identities (the 'what') rather than a free-floating scalar supports separating object identity from a raw resource snapshot.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Stimulus-specific value coding in OFC supports binding value TO identity, but does not show the brain SELECTS a single 'most-wanted' identity to seed a downstream goal latent; the selection/arg-max step is REE-specific. Medial vs lateral OFC dissociate value vs identity coding, so a single z_object seed conflates two anatomically separable codes.
mapping.source_context: Three male macaques, three-armed bandit with periodically replaced novel options; single-unit recording in OFC.

confidence_components.notes: Strong primate electrophysiology; mapping fidelity limited by the arg-max-over-identity selection step and medial/lateral subregion dissociation.
